intent: Adopt a licensed heavy armor base and distinguish the project light armor while preserving useful three-dimensional plates and native player poses
priority: Appearance and movement first, as requested by the user
device_and_renderer: Desktop Minecraft Java; native OpenGL client, standard cutout shading, no shader pack required
materials: Original pixel-painted albedo plus project purple crystals, alpha cutout and crystal-only fullbright glow mask; no PBR maps or environment dynamic lights

texture_plan.uv: Per-face atlas, no tiled material, preserve upstream artwork pixels
texture_plan.density: Authored armor density retained near 1 pixel/model-unit; small crystal facets share a low-frequency opaque 1-2 by 1-3 pixel patch

geometry_budget.note: Six quad faces per cube; emissive pass adds rendering work. Slot visibility limits each draw to its equipment part.

rig: Eight independent standard equipment bones, no unmapped waist/root wrapper; skirt halves follow respective thighs; boots follow feet slot
animation: Native HumanoidModel poses copied by GeoArmorRenderer, including body translations and arm/leg rotations; no authored animation clips
delivery: Editable MCP bbmodels, MCP geometry exports, exact-pixel runtime atlas and glow mask, matching four-slot item meshes, licenses and dual-client proof
verification: Native player front/back, walk, crouch, bow, riding, four individual slots, mixed sets, inventory and zero-light room; inspect actual screenshots and assert renderer slot visibility/pose correspondence
